newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Feb 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Gulf countries operating in the 'grace period' allowing developing countries under the Montreal Protocol to keep using CFCs will have to tighten their systems soon as time runs out.
- The Gulf Aircraft Maintenance Co (GAMCO) is planning to expand overseas by opening an office in Britain soon, a senior company official said.

- Saudi banks performed well in 1996, aided by rising internatioanl prices and domestic demand for credit. The rise in profitability was directly attributed to reduced interest expenses, which were down 10.3 percent and increased income from banking services, up 12.2 percent.
- Efforts are being made to develop Oman's Mina Raysut in southern Dhofar into a world-class container port.
- Granada Group Plc said it agreed to sell Welcome Break, a chain of 21 roadside service stations, to the Bahrain-based Investcorp for 476 million stg.
- A Saudi newspaper on Tuesday denounced Israeli Prime Minister Banjamin Netanyahu as a "racist" for saying Arabs should be educated about peace.

- The Lego Group has crafted scenes from the Arab World and launched a two-year roadshow which will arrive in the UAE next month in time fo the UAE shopping festival. The scenes include "The Oasis", "The Mosque" and "The Camel Race".
- UAE's GAMCO won a 180 million dirham deal for the maintenance of nine British Royal Air Force Lockheed Tristar jets.
